bull_bear.body: Deleveraging priority (Net debt down to INR 280cr). Final dividend INR 2/share declared. M&A focused on tourism assets (Chandon) and potential craft spirit brands. No buyback mentioned.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: Grape mix cost overhang persisting until next harvest (Q3FY27). EU FTA duty reduction (1 year out) threatening premium segment pricing power. Summer heat damaging retail inventory (lack of AC in trade). Unsustainable discounting by competitors in economy segment.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Cautiously Optimistic. Acknowledges margin pain as temporary/structural shift for quality. Aggressive on Tourism scaling ('laser focused'). Disciplined on M&A (waiting for right fit in spirits). Transparent on cost headwinds.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: The 'margin compression' is partly a quality upgrade story (using premium grapes in entry-level wines) which may boost long-term brand equity despite short-term P&L hit. Tourism revenue reported ex-wine sales in P&L, understating the true INR 110cr scale of the vertical. 75% renewable energy mix achieved; moving to battery storage to hedge power costs.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- "Healthy Balance Sheet with Debt-to-EBITDA at <3x (FY26)".
- Capital discipline framed through price paid and capex efficiency: the Domaine Rāsā estate acquired at "a highly attractive price of INR 20 crore", and 1 Mn litres of cellar capacity added in FY26 "at 33% lower capex".
- Working capital is an explicit constraint shaping operations — the shift to a higher mix of wine grapes versus table grapes is described as "aimed at conserving working capital", at the cost of ~150 bps of gross margin.
- Stated ambition: "Accelerating Earnings Growth over next 3 years (FY26-FY29) with improved EBITDA margins and capital efficiency".
- Long-run track record cited: "Delivered Revenue, Operating EBITDA and PAT CAGR of 6%, 11% and 52% over FY21-26"; the deck makes no mention of dividend policy or buybacks.
bull_bear.title: Capital allocation policy (investor deck)

bull_bear.body:
- Market leadership: over 60% share of India's domestic Elite & Premium wine market and market leader in every wine category
- Distribution scale: 25,000+ points of sale across India, plus growing Canteen Stores Department listings (9 to 14 in FY26) and modern trade/e-commerce presence
- Brand strength / digital reach: most followed wine company in India on social media (380K+ followers) across Instagram, Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube and X
- First-mover / pioneer positioning: launched India's first winery tasting room (2005), first vineyard resort (2010), and first wine-in-a-can (2020), shaping India's modern wine culture
- Wine tourism moat: Nashik campus is described as the most-visited vineyard destination globally (over 4 lakh annual visitors), with a hospitality portfolio of three resorts (154 keys) providing a differentiated, difficult-to-replicate asset base
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Regional/single-market demand concentration — FY26 revenue and profitability were materially impacted by transient disruptions confined to a small number of states — a route-to-market disruption in Telangana (the company's third-largest market) during H1 and one-time tactical destocking in Karnataka (its second-largest market) in Q3 — showing exposure to state-level, single-market shocks.
- Operating deleverage on demand softness — A 3.7% YoY revenue decline in FY26 (to Rs. 596.2 crore) produced a much larger 30.6% decline in Operating EBITDA and 672 bps of margin contraction (24.07% to 17.35%), with PAT falling 63.5%, indicating profitability is highly sensitive to relatively small swings in sales volume.
- Comparability distortion from one-off items — FY25 included a one-time WIPS unwinding gain of Rs. 10.4 crore that created a high base effect depressing FY26 YoY comparisons, illustrating how non-recurring items can materially skew reported growth and margins in a given year.
- Execution risk on pending wine-tourism acquisition — The agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre wine estate in Dindori is described as 'currently underway' with details to be shared 'upon transaction completion' — an unclosed M&A commitment with no disclosed timeline or completion certainty.
- Wine-tourism capacity absorption risk — Room capacity was expanded ~50% to 154 keys with the launch of The Haven by Sula; sustaining ~77% occupancy while continuing to add rooms is necessary to convert the added capacity into proportionate revenue growth.
- Agricultural/harvest dependency — Grape supply for winemaking depends on the annual harvest's quality and volume (Harvest 2026 was described as the sixth consecutive favourable vintage), exposing the business to weather and agri-climate variability inherent to viticulture.
- Leverage sensitivity to EBITDA volatility — Net Debt/EBITDA was reported below 3x (debt of Rs. 294 crore as of 31 March 2026), but FY26 EBITDA declined 30.6% YoY, meaning a further profitability decline would push leverage multiples higher from an already-reduced EBITDA base.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.title: Positioning (investor deck)

business.body:
- [Acquisition] Completion of the Chandon Estate purchase in Q1 FY27 and its rebranding to Domaine Rāsā is the deck's headline corporate event, opening the presentation ahead of performance highlights.
- [Geographic mix] Telangana, Haryana, Chandigarh, CSD and Exports delivered strong double-digit growth, while "Karnataka continues to remain soft; expect it to turn a corner in H2 FY27" — and the shortfall in core markets (Maharashtra & Karnataka) is named as a driver of adverse market mix on gross margin.
- [Multi-year trajectory] The FY21-FY26 revenue-from-operations series printed is 418 / 454 / 553 / 609 / 619 / 596 (INR Cr) with a stated 6% CAGR, i.e. FY26 revenue was below FY25; Operating EBITDA over the same span was 61 / 113 / 158 / 176 / 149 / 103 (INR Cr) at margins of 14.6% / 25.0% / 28.5% / 28.9% / 24.1% / 17.3%, and PAT was 3 / 52 / 84 / 93 / 70 / 26 (INR Cr). The FY26 figures show a marked step-down from the FY24 peak.
- [Wine tourism trajectory] Wine tourism revenue series of 18 / 35 / 45 / 55 / 60 / 73 (INR Cr) for FY21-FY26, a stated 32% CAGR — the fastest-growing disclosed line and the only one of the six charted series rising in FY26.

CSD listings expanding from 9 to 14 wines by Q4FY27. Potential entry into spirits/tequila via M&A (no target yet).
outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Continue to scale up nationwide distribution of The Source range further in FY27, building on the strategy of expanding its availability that paid off in FY26
- Continue the cost rationalization program into FY27 after operating expenses (including S&D) declined 2% YoY in FY26
- Invest most of capex over the next 3 years in expanding the wine tourism business, with a medium-term target to significantly expand the resort portfolio and room capacity
- Reduce wine inventory carryover and working capital consumption by shifting grape procurement mix toward wine grapes and away from open-market table grapes
- Advance sustainability agenda: shift focus from adding solar panels to adding battery energy storage systems for resilience against rising fuel and power costs
- Expand international presence, marked by entry into Dubai as a step toward building Sula's presence in an international, lifestyle-driven market
- Pursue targeted regional market expansion (e.g. Indore and other emerging regions) with region-specific engagement approaches
- Strengthen on-trade footprint through tie-ups with hospitality/F&B partners and expanded presence across marquee outlets
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: In FY26, Sula commissioned a new 1 million litre low-cost cellar at its Domaine Dindori unit (Maharashtra), built at 33% lower capex, dedicated to Economy & Popular brands, taking total winery capacity to 19.2 million litres. It also increased bottling capacity at two Maharashtra units (Nashik Winery and ND Wines facility), raising WIPS capture to ~100% in FY26 from ~85% in FY25. On the wine-tourism side, the company launched its 3rd resort, The Haven by Sula (50 keys, near York) in Q3 FY26, taking total room capacity to 154 keys, and commissioned a new tasting room and restaurant expansion at Domaine Sula (near Bengaluru) in January 2026. Management's stated Growth Strategy (FY26-FY29) targets accelerating earnings growth via six pillars: product development (new wine launches), sufficient capacity for growth, expanding market penetration (wider national availability of The Source and RASA, new defence listings, new markets), expanding wine tourism & D2C business, augmenting brand visibility, and strategic M&A. The company has signed a binding agreement to acquire Chandon's 19-acre wine estate in Dindori, Nashik, to expand its wine tourism footprint, with the transaction underway and further details to be shared on completion; it also intends to pursue further strategic investments and acquisitions in wine tourism and the Indian AlcoBev industry. On the ESG side, the company doubled its Battery Energy Storage System capacity to ~2,217 kW (~2 MW) and increased solar-powered irrigation pump capacity by 130 HP to a total of 253 HP, alongside continued solar PV capacity build-out (4,703 kWH installed) at its Maharashtra and Karnataka facilities.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Transient disruptions (Telangana route-to-market issue, Karnataka tactical destocking) are now largely behind the company, with demand trends improving across key markets entering FY27
- Own Brands showed a progressive recovery in Q4 FY26 (revenue +7.1% YoY, Own Brands +7% YoY) which management expects to carry into FY27
- Premiumization mix shift continues to be a driver, with Elite & Premium share rising to 78.4% of Own Brands in FY26, led by The Source range
- Wine Tourism is a structural growth driver, powered by double-digit footfall growth, room revenue growth and expanded resort capacity (154 keys after The Haven launch)
- A new retail license policy in Uttar Pradesh is expected to enable significant expansion in retail licenses, supporting another strong year for Sula in UP in FY27
- Expansion of CSD listings (9 to 14) is expected to support stronger CSD sales momentum in the second half of FY27
- A healthy Harvest 2026 (sixth consecutive favourable vintage) combined with enhanced storage capacity is expected to ensure adequate grape availability for FY27
- Shift in grape procurement mix toward wine grapes (~99% vs ~80% last year) reflects a conscious strategy to reduce inventory carryover and working capital consumption going into FY27

deepdive.thesis: Sula returned to top-line growth in Q4 (+7% YoY) driven by Wine Tourism (+17%) and elite brand recovery, though margins compressed due to a strategic shift to costlier wine grapes and a prior-year one-off gain. The strategic pivot toward high-margin hospitality (targeting >20% revenue mix) and the pending Chandon estate acquisition signal a structural re-rating from a pure-play winemaker to an integrated experiential luxury operator.
